summary: Describes how a presence user agent can publish only the changed parts of its presence information to a presence server using SIP. Normally every publication carries the complete state, even for a tiny change, which is wasteful for large presence documents. Sending just the differences makes updates smaller and cheaper.

eli5.summary: Instead of rewriting your whole status board every time one line changes, you just correct the one line and tell the server about it. That keeps your updates short and quick.

questions: how to publish presence changes only
how does sip publish update presence
subtitle: Let a SIP presence client publish only the parts of its status that changed instead of the whole document.

tldr.problem: Each SIP presence publication carries the full presence document, so a small change to a large document costs a lot of bandwidth, especially on slow or high-latency links.
tldr.mechanism: After an initial full-state publication, the client sends PUBLISH requests with the application/pidf-diff+xml type that carry add, replace and remove patch operations, which the server applies in order.
tldr.outcome: Updates can be much smaller. The server keeps only the patched result, so there is no rollback except by sending full state.

today: RFC 5264 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It depends on RFC 3903 and RFC 5262.

sections.title: The Problem with Full-State Publication
sections.content:
In SIP presence, a presence user agent (PUA) publishes a user's presence information, and a presence agent collects publications and builds the composite state. The baseline format is the Presence Information Data Format (PIDF, RFC 3863), an XML format that groups data into tuples.

With ordinary publication, every PUBLISH carries full state, however little has changed since the last one. For a sizeable document with small changes, that is inefficient, and low-bandwidth, high-latency links make it worse. This RFC lets the PUA publish only the changed parts after an initial full publication, using the partial PIDF format of RFC 5262.
sections.eli5: Sending your whole profile each time you change one word is wasteful. This lets you send just the changed word.

sections.title: How Partial Publication Works
sections.content:
Normal publication (RFC 3903) sends a SIP PUBLISH request to the presentity's address-of-record. The compositor stores the information and returns an entity-tag that identifies the publication. The PUA quotes that tag in later requests to refresh, modify or remove it. Information disappears when removed or when it expires.

For partial publication, the initial publication always carries full state. Later modifying publications may carry either deltas or full state. Both use the application/pidf-diff+xml content type, with a <pidf-full> root element for full state or a <pidf-diff> root for changes. A diff holds <add>, <replace> and <remove> operations.

Ordering comes from the entity-tags and conditional requests that PUBLISH already has. The RFC chose not to also use the version attribute of partial PIDF, because two versioning mechanisms could contradict each other. The compositor applies the patches in sequence and passes the result to its composition logic like any full publication. Expiration applies to the whole patched publication.
sections.eli5: You hand in your whole poster once. After that you only send sticky notes saying "add this", "change that" or "remove this", and the server updates the poster.

sections.title: What the Client Does
sections.content:
Supporting entities MUST support application/pidf-diff+xml as well as the baseline application/pidf+xml. Listing the partial type in an Accept header of a SIP response signals support. A PUA can learn this with an OPTIONS request or by trial and error, after a 415 error response.

To send full state, the PUA sets the Content-Type to application/pidf-diff+xml and uses a <pidf-full> root with an entity attribute naming the presentity, holding the children of a PIDF <presence> element. For a delta, the root is <pidf-diff> with the same attribute, containing patch operations that MUST be built in sequence as RFC 5262 defines.

The PUA SHOULD batch several patch operations into one PUBLISH to cut traffic. If the delta would be bigger than the full state, it SHOULD send full state instead, unless the sizes cannot be compared. If the first PUBLISH gets a 415 (Unsupported Media Type), the PUA SHOULD retry with application/pidf+xml.
sections.eli5: The sender first checks that the server understands sticky notes. If the notes would be bigger than the poster, it just sends the poster again.

sections.title: What the Server Does
sections.content:
For a <pidf-full> body, the compositor MUST take the received document as its local presence document, replacing any previous publications. For a <pidf-diff> body in a modifying publication (one with an If-Match header holding a valid entity-tag), it MUST apply the patch operations in sequence to its stored document.

A <pidf-diff> in an initial publication is not allowed, and the request MUST be rejected with an error such as 400 (Invalid Partial Publication).

If a partial publication expires without a refresh, the compositor MUST clear the entire full-state publication. It keeps no record of applied patches, so it cannot roll back to an earlier version.
sections.eli5: The server keeps one current copy and edits it. It does not keep the old versions, so if the notes stop coming, the whole poster comes down.

sections.title: Errors
sections.content:
If the compositor hits errors while processing a application/pidf-diff+xml document, it MUST reject the request with a 400 (Bad Request) response. It MAY include diagnostics in the body, using an error condition element from Section 5.1 of RFC 5261.

If any other error occurs before the whole partial publication, including all its patch operations, is processed, the compositor MUST reject the request with a 500 (Server Internal Error) response and revert to its original stored presence information.
sections.eli5: If one of the sticky notes is wrong, the server throws out the whole batch and keeps the poster as it was.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.content:
The RFC's example has two exchanges. First the PUA sends an initial PUBLISH with a <pidf-full> document holding three tuples, and receives a 200 OK with a SIP-ETag header. Then it sends a second PUBLISH with SIP-If-Match set to that tag and a <pidf-diff> body.

The diff adds a new tuple before the note element, replaces a tuple's basic status with open, removes a busy activity and replaces a contact priority with 0.7. The compositor applies them in order and replies 200 OK with a new entity-tag.
sections.eli5: First you hand in the full poster and get a ticket number. Then you show the ticket and send a few edits, and you get a new ticket number back.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: This specification relies on the behavior defined in RFC 3903, and all the security considerations of Event State Publication apply in their entirety. The RFC states that it adds no new security considerations.
sections.eli5: The safety rules are the same as for ordinary publishing, and this adds none of its own.

items.title: replace
items.text: Replaces elements or attributes whose content changed.
